title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
summary: ActionOPD replaces offline imitation and token-level on-policy distillation with action-level on-policy distillation, rewarding student actions by semantic agreement with sampled teacher actions, so teacher token probabilities and shared tokenization are no longer required. It costs an on-policy RL training loop with sampling from both student and teacher at each state, which is substantially more compute- and orchestration-intensive than offline supervised fine-tuning, though the teacher can be a black-box API. It can fail if the sampled teacher actions are unrepresentative or the semantic-agreement reward is noisy, and the gains are demonstrated only on curated tool-use tasks, so transfer to other agent workloads is unverified.
rationale: The method fits constrained infrastructure by allowing a black-box API teacher and small students, but the on-policy RL training cost and task-specific evidence base justify a small-scale pilot rather than direct adoption.

Average gains of 3.3-6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks for Qwen3-4B/8B students; competitive with offline distillation and token-level OPD on τ²-bench.
